# Results — Study 51 (Blue-Chip): the quality (gross-profitability) premium

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). **Gross profitability = gross profit ÷
total assets** from SEC EDGAR 10-K filings, and aligned next-year total returns (Yahoo), for current
S&P 500 members. Annual long high-GP / short low-GP. As-of the EDGAR pull; inputs fingerprint
`184218d2df5c`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · "Quality premium is real"? `SUPPORTED`

Quality — profitable firms out-earning unprofitable ones (Novy-Marx 2013) — is the factor that *survived*
where size and value faded, and on our data it points the right way: the long-high/short-low gross-
profitability hedge earns **+3.3%/yr (hit 61%)**, high-GP firms (+19.3%) beat low-GP (+16.0%). But it's
`WEAK` and `FRAGILE` on what we can measure: the Sharpe is **0.20 (t ≈ 0.8)** — not significant — over
just **~18 years**, because SEC XBRL filings only reach back to ~2007, *missing* the strong pre-2008
quality decades. The sign and the literature both say `SUPPORTED`; our short, survivorship-biased,
large-cap sample can't *confirm* it strongly. A real factor we can only glimpse here.

## Data stamp

- **Universe**: ~150 current S&P 500 members reporting GrossProfit, ~2007–2025 (XBRL era), fingerprint
  `184218d2df5c` (survivorship-biased, large-cap, short sample — all stated)

## The quality long-short — positive, but modest

| | annual return |
|---|---|
| high-GP leg (long) | +19.3% |
| low-GP leg (short) | +16.0% |
| **hedge (high − low)** | **+3.3%** |
| equal-weight universe | +19.6% |

| | hedge |
|---|---|
| Sharpe | **0.20** |
| t-stat (~18 years) | **0.8** |
| hit rate | **61%** |

The direction is right and the hit rate is above a coin flip, but the magnitude is small and the t-stat
doesn't clear significance. High-GP firms beat low-GP ones by ~3 pts/year — real, but not the powerful
edge the long history shows.

## Why we can only glimpse it

1. **The XBRL window is too short.** SEC machine-readable fundamentals start ~2007, so we miss the
   1963–2007 decades where Novy-Marx documents the strongest quality premium. ~18 annual observations
   give a t of ~0.8 even for a real effect.
2. **Survivorship + large-cap.** Current S&P 500 members are the survivors, and quality matters more in
   the broader, riskier cross-section. Both bias the *test*, not the factor.
3. **Quality's home is "junk", relatively.** The premium is sharpest shorting low-quality, often
   smaller, distressed names — under-represented in a large-cap survivor set.

## The honest takeaway

Gross-profitability quality is `WEAK` and `FRAGILE` *on this data* — positive (+3.3%/yr, 61% hit) and the
right sign, but a Sharpe of 0.20 (t ≈ 0.8) over a short XBRL sample can't confirm the strong premium the
literature documents. So `SUPPORTED` in direction, unconfirmed in magnitude — the factor that survived,
seen through a too-small window. Unlike the inverted lottery/idio-vol studies, quality at least *points
the right way* on large caps.
